answer: One sybil defense targets the one-mind-many-masks attack by correlating behavior across identities. Honest agents scatter like a nebula of distinct styles and latencies, but masks fed by a single inference pipeline cluster tightly, their answers as alike as two halves of one walnut. So the network sends each identity on a solo voyage: a randomized-deadline capability chain where each task unlocks only when the prior one finishes. A shared backend must run every mask's chain in sequence, so sustaining N aliases costs N times the GPUs, turning cheap masks into a real hardware bill.
